newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria cenbank sees early EMU membership - paper.
newsitem.headline: Austria cenbank sees early EMU membership - paper.

text.p: Austrian central bank chief Klaus Liebscher is convinced that Austria would be among the first wave of countries to join Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU), the Kurier newspaper reported on Monday.

"I am convinced that we will take part in the first round," Liebscher told the paper in an interview. He added that it would not be a "misfortune" if only selected members of the European Union would make it into EMU on time in 1999.
"Many of the countries that will probably not take part in the first group are economically and politically important to us," the central bank chief said.
"But I don't see a small euro-zone as a misfortune, it would rather be a signal for other countries to join as quickly as possible," he added.
There has been increased debate over the past weeks whether Austria's second-biggest trading partner Italy will be able to qualify for early membership in the single currency.
Liebscher said the chances that EMU will start on time were between 80 and 85 percent. "The rest depends on the development of Germany and France," he added.
